title: Microsoft Purview DLP: upgraded inline protection for Microsoft Entra-managed apps in Edge for Business
notes: claim 61: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the browser-version prerequisite is out of date; Microsoft Learn now specifies version 158, not 144. The claim that users notice protection only when a rule blocks or audits an action also overlooks work-profile prompts. The roadmap facts are accurate, but licensing guidance and the abbreviated control paths need clarification.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has published no licence specific to this upgrade.
claims.quote: With a DLP policy, admins can apply inline data protection to identify, audit, and protect sensitive data in interactions with cloud apps (unmanaged and managed) in Microsoft Edge for Business.
claims.fix: The upgrade-specific gap understates published entitlement for the existing capability. Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and opening licensing sentence with: 'Browser inline DLP is included in Microsoft 365 E5/A5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5 Information Protection and Governance, and Office 365 E5/A5. No licensing change specific to this upgrade is published at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-data-loss-prevention-dlp-for-cloud-apps-in-the-browser. In the cost rationale replace 'a licence for this upgrade is not yet published' with 'a licensing change specific to this upgrade is not yet published'. Replace the licensing open question with 'Will this upgrade change the published browser DLP entitlement, including for simulation mode or added alerting?'

claims.claim: Managed-app policy scope is reached in the Purview portal through Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Enterprise apps and Devices > Custom > Custom policy > Managed cloud apps.
claims.quote: Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. Select Enterprise apps and Devices. Select Custom from the Categories list and then Custom policy from the Regulations list. Accept the default Full directory on the Assign admin units page. Select Managed cloud apps
claims.fix: The printed steps are correct but omit the default admin-unit page and stop before the scope selectors. Replace the path with 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Enterprise apps and Devices > Custom > Custom policy > Assign admin units > Full directory > Managed cloud apps'. Add to the note: 'Select Specific users and groups > + Include > Include groups to choose groups; select + Include managed apps to choose apps. Groups must first be imported from connected apps.' Use the same path and note in the rendered table. These steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-prevent-cloud-sharing-from-edge-biz.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for the app and user scope of today's managed-app browser DLP policy.
claims.quote: Searched: managed cloud apps PowerShell DLP policy browser. Read New-DlpCompliancePolicy and Set-DlpCompliancePolicy for browser, managed apps, locations and scope: Browser is specified for unmanaged apps; no managed-browser scope operation was identified.

claims.claim: Edge browser enforcement is configured in the Defender portal at System > Settings > Cloud apps > Conditional Access App Control > Edge for Business protection.
claims.quote: go to System > Settings > Cloud apps > Conditional Access App Control section > Edge for Business protection.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct settings page but stops before the enforcement control. Extend it to 'System > Settings > Cloud apps > Conditional Access App Control > Edge for Business protection > Enforce usage of Edge for Business > Allow access only from Edge'. Add to the note: 'Turn on Edge for Business browser protection must be On; set Enforce for which devices? to All devices for the managed-app DLP setup.' Update the rendered table identically. The control is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-cloud-apps/in-browser-protection and the all-device requirement at the already cited managed-app setup page.

claims.claim: Users notice protection only when a rule blocks or audits an action in Edge for Business.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to check controls that have no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Check that each app is onboarded to Conditional Access app control with a custom session control ... List users who are also in scope for Defender session policies or Endpoint DLP policies ... Review rule matches in Defender XDR investigations. Table: Purview scope; Edge enforcement.
claims.fix: Do not add rows. Replace the second Before rollout bullet with 'Check that Edge for Business in-browser protection is on (row 2), so you know which gaps the upgrade must not widen.' Remove the third Before rollout bullet and the first After rollout bullet. Replace the remaining After rollout bullet with 'Re-check in-browser protection settings after any policy change, because the browser policy depends on them.' The table lacks rows for Conditional Access onboarding/session controls, overlapping Defender and Endpoint policies, and investigation monitoring; the factual explanations can remain in the body.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The prose reports an absent tenant-wide upgrade switch that the controls table does not represent.
claims.quote: No tenant-wide switch for the upgraded experience is documented at the time of writing. The table contains only managed-app policy scope and Edge browser enforcement.
claims.fix: Remove the final sentence 'No tenant-wide switch for the upgraded experience is documented at the time of writing.' The standard requires a both-null row for a switch reported absent, but a correction must not add rows; the narrower general statement that upgrade-specific controls are not documented can remain.
